subject: physical-education
title: Correction and reflection: reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use under transfer
focus: reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use
essentialQuestion: What can I now do, and what am I choosing to carry forward?
materials: Optional: two soft household objects may mark a path. Floor tape, cones, a track, and a gym are not required.
Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
movementCues: Begin in a ready position with a balanced base, soft knees, eyes up, and the travel path clear.
Move with quiet, controlled steps or wheel pushes and keep enough room to stop without crossing the boundary.
Change direction by slowing first, lowering the center of control, and pushing smoothly into the new path.
Finish under control inside the space; smooth starts, stops, and spacing matter more than speed.
Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
ageAppropriateTechnique: Self-manage the task by rehearsing at low intensity, changing one variable at a time, and choosing control and repeatable technique over a maximal result.
spaceSetup: Clear a dry, non-slip area at least two arm-spans wide when available. Mark the boundary with visible household objects or imaginary lines, remove furniture, cords, pets, and breakables, and keep a stable chair or wall nearby if support helps. Low-space path: clear one arm-span while seated or standing and keep every movement in place.

optional: Optional: two soft household objects may mark a path. Floor tape, cones, a track, and a gym are not required.
householdSubstitutes: Use only soft, unbreakable household items that a trusted adult approves; imaginary equipment and paper planning are always valid substitutes.
equipmentRequirements.equalCreditNoEquipment: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm patterns to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions, then name the cue that kept the movement controlled.

safetyRules: Check the floor, ceiling, footwear or mobility supports, boundary, and any optional item before moving. Keep people, pets, furniture, cords, and breakables outside the boundary.
Use a self-selected easy-to-moderate challenge, breathe continuously, and choose control over speed, force, distance, or repetition.
Rest, reduce range or pace, use support, or choose the non-movement planning path at any time without losing credit.
Keep the pace below running indoors unless a trusted adult has approved a larger clear area. Use no jumping when the surface, ceiling, footwear, or balance support is uncertain.
stoppingRules: Stop immediately for pain, dizziness, unusual breathing difficulty, a head impact, or any movement that feels unsafe; tell a trusted adult.
Stop when a person, pet, object, or slippery surface enters the movement area. Reset the area before continuing.
After a head impact, injury, or symptoms that do not settle with rest, do not resume the activity until a trusted adult or qualified professional says it is safe.
accessibleAdaptation: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit.
lowSpaceNoEquipmentAlternative: Equal-credit low-space option: travel in place or use seated arm patterns to show start, pathway change, controlled stop, and spacing decisions, then name the cue that kept the movement controlled.
activitySteps: Setup: read the equipment, space, safety, and stop rules; clear the area and choose the standard or adapted path.
Prepare: begin with comfortable joint movements and an easy version of the lesson pattern while breathing normally.

Practice: apply the movement cues for reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use at a self-selected easy-to-moderate challenge, resting or reducing the range whenever control changes.
Apply: show, describe, draw, sign, or write one controlled example of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use, including the cue or decision that made it work.
Finish: transition to easy movement or rest, then name one safety check and one adjustment for next time. No score, measurement, photo, or recording is needed.
privacySafeScenario: Assemble and present the portfolio to one trusted adult: category evidence, a training principle explained, the revised safety plan, and a justified plan for Grade 10.
studentTask: Learner works reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use assembled into the portfolio itself and defended against a question the learner did not prepare for at a self-set intensity, then records what held, what degraded first, and how this occasion differed from the earlier one.
knowledgeCheck: In one concise response, say which feature of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use degraded first under the added demand, why, and what you would change before the next attempt.
completionCriteria: The learner clears or accurately describes the safe space and selects the standard, accessible, or no-equipment path for reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use.

The learner completes or fully describes one controlled practice-and-application sequence using at least one stated movement cue; stopping or resting for safety still counts as responsible completion.
The learner identifies the equipment choice (including none), one safety or stop rule, and one technique adjustment or next step.
A seated, supported, reduced-range, solo, low-space, or no-equipment version earns the same credit when it demonstrates the same cue and decision.
adaptationChoices: Use the same cues while seated, supported by a stable chair or wall, using a mobility aid, working through a comfortable reduced range, or describing/gesturing the movement when movement is not appropriate. Work solo or with one trusted adult. The adapted path is assessed for the same control, decision, and explanation and earns equal credit.
extensionChallenge: Design the next progression of reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use yourself, or coach the transfer condition to someone else so that they succeed with it — without completing another learner's graded work.
accessibilitySupports: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, demonstrated, or described responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, rest-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, or response mode.
Every movement task has a seated, supported, reduced-range, reduced-pace, and solo version that reaches the same standard.
Presentation may be spoken one-to-one, written, or submitted as an annotated document. No recording, video, photograph, or audience beyond one adult is required.

optionalReflection.prompt: Invite the learner to notice where reviewing the safety and stop-rule plan against a year of use shows up outside the session under real conditions. No purchase, account creation, photograph, recording, or public performance is required.

neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
This task never requires maximal effort, exercise as punishment, or movement through pain.
This task never requires gym access, specialized equipment, or a purchase; the no-equipment path earns equal credit.
